open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:`source_folder`
open_points.text:
deciding whether a requested name passes condition 1 of A3 rule 5, and reading that file once without
  following a link;
open_points.question: What module owns the immutable result of this one read, and must that result contain the bytes, computed source id, modification time, and the A1/condition-1 outcome so that `photo_delivery` and `photo_preparation` never reopen the source?
options: `source_folder` owns and returns one immutable read snapshot containing all required observations
`source_folder` returns a handle or partial result and another module completes hashing, metadata capture, or preparation
`source_folder` invokes downstream preparation while it controls the secure open
open_points.default_guess: `source_folder` returns one immutable snapshot with bytes, source id, modification time, and a lower-level rejection outcome; `photo_delivery` maps that outcome and passes the same bytes to preparation.

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:`source_folder`
open_points.text: - how the four lower modules are combined into one operation;
open_points.question: What is the authoritative direct dependency between `photo_delivery` and `source_folder`, and which public symbols cross it?
options: A shared abstraction or result provider sits between them
open_points.default_guess: Declare a direct `photo_delivery` → `source_folder` dependency using the two candidate capabilities, with no reverse edge.

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:`source_folder`
open_points.text: - the modification time of a file in the service's time form.
open_points.question: For delivery, is the modification time the value read from the path while condition 1 is checked, or the value obtained from the securely opened file whose bytes are actually hashed and prepared?
options: Use the pre-open path-metadata value from condition 1
Use metadata from the opened file corresponding to the bytes read
Require both observations to agree and fail if they differ
open_points.default_guess: Use metadata from the securely opened file corresponding to the bytes read.

witness.initial: An ordinary image has no usable camera date and path modification time T1.
events: `source_folder` reads path metadata while checking condition 1.
Syncthing replaces the path with another regular file having modification time T2 before the secure open.
`source_folder` opens and reads the replacement once; preparation must fall back to a modification time.
outcomes: The publication body uses T1 because condition-1 path metadata is the owned modification time.
The publication body uses T2 because metadata is taken from the opened file whose bytes were delivered.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different `photo_date`, and the owner or client later sees different date ordering in the Portal.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text:
After condition 5 a stored image may remain without a record: no caller has received
   its reference, and a repeated delivery of the same file writes it again and completes the placement.
open_points.question: Does “the same file” mean the same source content and source id under any currently valid name, or the same filesystem name or file identity used by the failed attempt?
options: Any ordinary file with the same content and source id can complete the placement
Only a retry using the same relative name can complete it
Only the same filesystem object can complete it
open_points.default_guess: Treat sameness as source content within the project, consistent with placement identity.

witness.initial: Writing the stored image succeeds, writing its placement record fails, and the original source is then renamed without changing its bytes.
events: The caller retries with the new ordinary relative name and the same source id.
The service finds no placement record and evaluates the named source.
outcomes: The retry reads the renamed file, rewrites the stored image, and completes the placement because the content identity is the same.
The retry does not qualify as the promised repeated delivery because the name or filesystem object differs, so completion requires the original file identity.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees either a completed placement or a failure/non-completing retry.
